edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 21 November 2026 and 10:00 AM IST on 22 November 2026

items.caseName: Radiant Inn Private Limited & Anr. v. Registrar of Companies, Mumbai
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member); Arun Baroka and Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: Owning a leasehold asset alone does not justify restoring a struck-off company, says NCLAT
items.text: The NCLAT upheld NCLT Mumbai's refusal to restore Radiant Inn, struck off in 2018. The company had filed no financial statements or annual returns after FY 2013-14 and said it did not plan to resume business. The tribunal held that missed service of Form STK-1 and a 95-year MIDC leasehold in Nagpur did not make restoration 'otherwise just', especially since no creditor or authority had asked for it.

items.caseName: MD Varadarajan v. Pharmarule
items.coram: Justice N. Seshasayee (Judicial Member) and Jatindranath Swain (Technical Member)
items.headline: Time spent before the Madras High Court excluded under Section 14 of the Limitation Act; NCLAT condones delay in IBC appeal
items.text: A suspended director of Kniss Laboratories challenged the August 2026 order admitting the company into CIRP, but first sought Article 227 relief in the Madras High Court. The NCLAT held that the time spent there can be excluded under Section 14 of the Limitation Act, which is different from condoning delay. It condoned the 15-day delay and listed the appeal for 23 November.

items.caseName: Satyendra Prasad Khorania, Resolution Professional of Sitaram Prints Private Limited
items.coram: Shammi Khan (Judicial Member) and Sanjeev Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: A 100% CoC vote does not exempt a resolution plan from Section 30(2) scrutiny: NCLT Ahmedabad sends plan back
items.text: The tribunal remitted a Rs. 60 lakh resolution plan, offered against financial creditor claims of about Rs. 618.9 crore, for reconsideration. It pointed to valuation discrepancies, a NIL valuation of receivables with no explanation, and missing details of Bank of Baroda's earlier SARFAESI sale. It sent these issues to the CoC and extended the CIRP by 30 days, to 20 December 2026.

items.caseName: Oldenburgische Landesbank AG v. Satyendra P. Khorania & Ors.
items.caseNo: IA No. 997 of 2023 in CP(IB) No. 38 of 2020
items.coram: Chitra Hankare (Judicial Member) and Dr. VG Venkata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: German indemnity cover no ground to cut lender's claim: NCLT Ahmedabad admits Oldenburgische Landesbank's full claim against Sumeet Industries
items.text: In an order dated 18 November, the tribunal set aside the RP's partial rejection of the German bank's claim in the CIRP of Sumeet Industries. It held that indemnity received under Germany's Buyer Credit Guarantee Scheme does not by itself justify reducing the claim, since the bank may enforce the subrogated rights and recoveries go to the German government. The monitoring committee was directed to admit the full claim of about EUR 8.28 million.

items.caseName: Unmesh Manohar Joshi v. IL&FS Financial Services Limited
items.caseNo: IA (I.B.C) Nos. 2353/MB/2024 and 4085/MB/2024 in CP (IB) No. 708/MB/2022
items.coram: Ashish Kalia (Judicial Member) and Banwari Lal Meena (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Mumbai rejects personal guarantor's challenge to RP report in Rs. 260 crore IL&FS debt case
items.text: In an order dated 20 November 2026, the tribunal dismissed two applications seeking to quash the Section 99 report and replace the RP. It found the RP had complied with Section 99 and had not breached any interim orders of the Supreme Court or NCLAT. Email service was held valid because the guarantor had acknowledged receiving the report at the same address.

items.caseName: Kushal Finnovation Capital Pvt. Ltd. v. Neelamber Agrotech Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Sushil Mahadeorao Kochey (Judicial Member) and Prabhat Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: A criminal complaint for cheating or forgery neither proves nor disproves a financial debt: NCLT Mumbai admits CIRP
items.text: In an order dated 20 November 2026, the tribunal held that criminal allegations run separately from insolvency proceedings and do not decide whether a financial debt exists. A Section 10 notice served by the debtor, with nothing to show the application was actually filed, was held not to admit liability. Finding debt and default proved, the tribunal admitted the Section 7 petition, appointed an IRP and declared a moratorium.

items.caseName: Southern Power Distribution Company of Telangana Limited v. Kondapalli Venkata Srinivas, Resolution Professional of BTT Industries Pvt. Ltd.
items.caseNo: IA (IBC) No. 1574 of 2025 in CP (IB) No. 341/7/HDB/2019
items.coram: Rajeev Bhardwaj (Judicial Member) and Sanjay Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: An RP appointed late must still preserve records received from the predecessor: NCLT Hyderabad
items.text: In an order dated 20 November, the tribunal partly allowed TSSPDCL's plea for the corporate debtor's records under Regulation 39A of the CIRP Regulations. It found that the panchnama the RP relied on had no itemised inventory and did not show that all the records were handed over. It ordered the records produced within four weeks, while clarifying that the duty does not cover every record from before or during the CIRP.

items.caseName: NTPC Limited v. Purusottam Behera, Liquidator of IVRCL Limited
items.caseNo: IA (IBC) No. 982 of 2025 in CP (IB) No. 294/7/HDB/2017
items.coram: Rajeev Bhardwaj (Judicial Member) and Sanjay Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Hyderabad condones NTPC's 408-day delay and directs IVRCL liquidator to verify Rs. 120.23 crore claim
items.text: In an order dated 20 November, the tribunal held that a liquidator has no power of its own to condone delay but must still verify a claim and communicate a decision. A creditor cannot be left uncertain indefinitely. The delay was condoned, NTPC was given 15 days to file supporting documents, and the liquidator was told to decide within 30 days after that.

items.caseName: Deepak Sarupariya, Resolution Professional of Spicy Entertainment and Media Limited v. Bombay Stock Exchange Limited
items.coram: Labh Singh (Judicial Member) and Rekha Kantilal Shah (Technical Member)
items.headline: Res judicata does not bar RP's refund claim that SAT never decided on merits: NCLT directs BSE to refund Rs. 39.6 lakh
items.text: In an order dated 20 November 2026, the tribunal rejected BSE's objection because SAT had dismissed the earlier appeal without ruling on the refund claim. It held that BSE could not adjust the money against pre-CIRP dues during the Section 14 moratorium and must file its claim with the RP instead. BSE was directed to refund the amount within two weeks.

items.caseName: ICSA (India) Ltd. v. National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. & Ors.
items.caseNo: IA (IBC) No. 131 of 2026 in CP (IB) No. 132/7/HDB/2019
items.coram: Rajeev Bhardwaj (Judicial Member) and Sanjay Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: Existing shares of a company sold as a going concern in liquidation can be extinguished without compensation: NCLT Hyderabad
items.text: On the successful bidder's application, the tribunal held in an order dated 20 November that ICSA's existing equity shares, held by promoters and the public, stand extinguished without consideration. It declined to cancel demat holdings, issue a new ISIN or waive listing fees, holding that these are matters of securities law. The bidder was given liberty to approach the relevant authorities.

items.caseName: Magnus Consulting Private Limited v. Anil Kashi Drolia, Resolution Professional of Renaissance Urban Infra Pvt. Ltd.
items.caseNo: IA (IBC) No. 1609/MB/2026 in IA (IBC) No. 4942/MB/2023 in CP (IB) No. 308/MB/2022
items.coram: K.R. Saji Kumar (Judicial Member) and Anil Raj Chellan (Technical Member)
items.headline: A party told its reply was defective cannot blame e-filing portal glitches, says NCLT Mumbai, but recalls forfeiture on terms
items.text: In an order dated 19 November, the tribunal rejected the explanation that the portal did not show the defects, noting the party knew its reply had been marked defective and had been given a final two weeks to correct it. Using its inherent powers under Rule 11 of the NCLT Rules, it still set aside the order forfeiting the right to reply in the preferential-transaction proceedings. The reply will be accepted if it shows as defect-free on the DMS portal within two weeks.

items.caseName: State Tax Officer (1), Unit-4, Ahmedabad v. Liquidator of Camson Bio Technologies Limited
items.coram: Sunil Kumar Aggarwal (Judicial Member) and Radhakrishna Sreepada (Technical Member)
items.headline: A statutory VAT charge does not make the State tax department a secured creditor: NCLT Bengaluru applies 2026 IBC amendment
items.text: In an order dated 23 October, the tribunal held that a charge created by operation of law is not a 'security interest' under the IBC. It treated the Explanation added to Section 3(31) by the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 as retrospective, which limits the Rainbow Papers ruling. It dismissed the department's Section 42 appeal over a Rs. 1.63 crore GVAT/CST claim that had been filed 418 days late.

items.caseName: Karnation Fund-I v. Gigu Hospitality Private Limited
items.coram: Sunil Kumar Aggarwal (Judicial Member) and Radhakrishna Sreepada (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Bengaluru directs operator of Gilly's Resto Bar to redeem Rs. 3 crore debentures within four weeks
items.text: In an order dated 22 October, the tribunal allowed the fund's petition under Section 71(10) of the Companies Act, 2013. The 1,200 unlisted debentures matured in December 2025, and only about Rs. 46 lakh of the roughly Rs. 3.32 crore maturity amount had been repaid. The company neither replied nor appeared, so the tribunal proceeded ex parte.

items.caseName: JMV Enterprise & Ors. v. Commissioner of Customs, Mundra
items.coram: Somesh Arora (Judicial Member) and Satendra Vikram Singh (Technical Member)
items.headline: Test reports on live consignments cannot fix duty liability on past imports: CESTAT Ahmedabad
items.text: The tribunal set aside duty demands, interest and confiscation for past fabric imports. It found the statements relied on had not been shown to be admissible under Section 138B, and no independent evidence linked goods recovered from buyers to the earlier shipments. It upheld the classification, anti-dumping duty and confiscation for the live consignments, reduced the penalties, and partly allowed the appeals.

items.caseName: M/s SKB Enterprises
items.headline: CESTAT strikes down bank guarantee condition for provisional release of imported walnut kernels
items.text: Customs had seized walnut kernels classified under CTH 0802 3200, and an order of 1 April 2026 made a differential-duty bank guarantee a condition of provisional release. The tribunal held the bank guarantee requirement was unwarranted on the facts and set it aside. The appeal was allowed on condition that the importer produces an end-use certificate.

items.caseName: Trishul Asphalt Products
items.headline: A GST appeal cannot be rejected just because pre-deposit was paid from the credit ledger instead of the cash ledger: GSTAT
items.text: The appellant had filed its first appeal under the amnesty scheme in Notification No. 53/2023 but paid the pre-deposit through the electronic credit ledger. The tribunal treated the wrong ledger as a curable defect. It held that technical portal difficulties cannot be used to defeat the statutory right of appeal.

items.caseName: Powerlite Generator Systems Private Limited
items.headline: Multiple e-way bills for the same transaction do not justify a GST penalty without proof of a violation: GSTAT
items.text: Three old generators moving from Haryana to Hyderabad were intercepted at Agra, and a Rs. 2.16 lakh penalty was imposed because earlier invoices and e-way bills had also been generated for two of them. The tribunal quashed the penalty. It noted that valid documents accompanied the goods and there was no evidence of an actual GST violation.

items.caseName: Rekha Khaitan
items.headline: ITAT gives partial relief on unexplained jewellery addition in Gautam Khaitan group search case
items.text: About 14 kg of jewellery worth roughly Rs. 7.64 crore was seized in a January 2019 search of the group. The tribunal took into account the allowance under CBDT Instruction No. 1916 (1994), which applies only within its permitted limits, and granted partial relief. It sustained an addition of Rs. 38.60 lakh under Section 69B.

items.caseName: M/s Bansal Industries
items.headline: Whether an arahtia is kachha or pucca depends on each transaction's terms: ITAT deletes Section 271B penalty
items.text: The AO treated the agricultural-produce dealer as a pucca arahtia and added Rs. 16.24 crore of agency sales to turnover, which triggered the tax-audit requirement and a Rs. 1.5 lakh penalty under Section 271B. The tribunal held that the classification turns on the terms of each transaction and that the dealer had a bona fide basis for leaving out agency sales. It deleted the penalty, finding reasonable cause under Section 273B.

items.caseName: Jitendrabhai Kacharabhai Thakor
items.headline: A cash balance shown in a pre-demonetisation return cannot be rejected on suspicion: ITAT deletes Rs. 66 lakh addition
items.text: The AO treated Rs. 66 lakh of the assessee's Rs. 1.82 crore cash deposits for AY 2017-18 as unexplained under Section 68. The tribunal held that a closing cash balance disclosed in a return filed before demonetisation cannot be disregarded on mere apprehension. It deleted the addition.
